correctness.rationale: The fibre of the continuous affine pushforward map over an extreme invariant measure is a nonempty compact convex face. Krein--Milman provides an extreme point of that fibre, and the face property makes it extreme among all shift-invariant trajectory-space measures, hence ergodic. Continuous-time Birkhoff and disintegration over the evaluation map then give the almost-everywhere existence of a trajectory with time average equal to the integral. In the circle counterexample, the two sign components are disjoint periodic shift orbits, each has a unique Haar invariant measure, all shift-invariant measures on their union are their convex combinations, and both project to the same Haar measure; the half-half lift is therefore nonergodic while its base marginal is the unique, hence extreme, invariant measure.

originality.rationale: The source itself is the closest possible comparison. Under Definition 3.2, fine ergodicity is stated relative to a displayed lift, while Theorem 3.7 attempts to infer extremality of that lift from extremality of its pushforward. The two-direction circle trajectory space is an explicit counterexample to that chosen-lift implication. The surviving existential repair is the precise affine-image theorem: an extreme base measure has at least one ergodic lift. Ordinary factor-map literature records the analogous existence of ergodic lifts, but no checked source states the sharp failure/repair for Suda's non-deterministic evaluation-map framework or draws the resulting partial answer to its time-average question.
residual_risks: The positive existential lift statement is a standard compact-convex consequence; originality rests on the sharp application/correction, explicit counterexample, and time-average consequence in Suda's framework rather than on a new convexity lemma.

A future revision of the preprint could redefine fine ergodicity existentially, in which case the positive repair would align with the intended theorem; the counterexample still shows that the displayed-lift reading and proof step are invalid.

value.rationale: The distinction is structurally important because the source uses fine ergodicity to import Birkhoff information from trajectory space. The counterexample pinpoints the exact failure of a central extremality theorem under its literal witness-dependent definition, while the face argument supplies the strongest valid replacement and yields a concrete partial answer to the paper's stated time-average question. This is a motivated boundary/correction, not a renaming or a numerical special case.
